reason: No keyboard we link places in the top three for a full-size low-profile mechanical board with a number pad, so a page would have to bend the ranking. Our only candidates are Lofree's 100-key boards; the Gamakay TK101 has a number pad but is not low-profile. All reads 2026-11-26 unless dated otherwise. (1) Price: the Keychron K5 Ultra 8K is $86.99 (100% layout, 2,600 mAh / up to 370 h, 8,000 Hz, hot-swappable; keychron.com store search record, the product page itself returned HTTP 429/500 to me) and the K5 Max is $71.24 for its lowest variant, $86.24 as the page displays (108 keys, 23.5 mm rear height with keycaps, about 95 h backlight off, 'stocked in the US warehouse', 2-5 day delivery; https://www.keychron.com/products/keychron-k5-max-qmk-via-wireless-custom-mechanical-keyboard). Both undercut the Lofree Flow Lite 2 100 at $119.00 on the page, $95.20 after the 20% cart discount (cart figure from the 11-21 cart test; the 'Black Friday Month · Keyboards 20% off' banner was still up today; https://www.lofree.co/products/flow-lite-2-100-low-profile-mechanical-keyboard). (2) Stock: the Lofree page reads 'Ships from Dec 1, in order placed'. (3) Layout: Lofree's tech specs list the board as '100 (96%)', though its description calls it 'the full-size 100-key layout'. (4) Its rated battery is 100 h (Bluetooth, lights off) and no named reviewer has measured it. So it places on neither price nor stock, the two grounds the desk notes allowed. Third place goes to the NuPhy Air100 V3 (99 keys, 4,000 mAh, up to 1,000 h RGB off, 3.5 ms latency measured by HLPlanet, https://www.hlplanet.com/?p=8737; RTINGS points number-pad buyers to it, https://www.rtings.com/keyboard/reviews/best/low-profile) or the Logitech MX Mechanical ($142.99, 'In stock. Ready to ship'; RTINGS tested the full-size unit; https://www.logitech.com/en-us/shop/p/mx-mechanical.920-010547). The Flow Lite 2 100 lands fourth or fifth: lightest (625 g) and narrowest (374 mm) of the field, which is a segment win, not a top-three place. The other Lofree number-pad boards do no better: Flow 2 100 is $169.00 on the page and PCWorld gave it 3/5 for a cramped number pad (angle E's read); Flow100 is being discontinued and has no 2.4 GHz, with RTINGS calling its wireless performance 'exceptionally poor' (angle C and E reads); Flow Lite100 is $109.00 on the page with no test at this size. An Amazon route for the Keychron pick could not be set up: amzcheck search returned nothing, amzcheck asin returned blocked for every ASIN, and amazon.com returned HTTP 503, so the listings are unopened (ASIN leads from search-result titles only: K5 Ultra 8K B0GV4NCLRZ, K5 Max hot-swap RGB Brown B0DCNR5VJY). Not read today: NuPhy's store price (nuphy.com HTTP 429; $149.95 is HLPlanet's figure) and the Logitech spec sections (did not load). If a verified Amazon record for the K5 Ultra 8K or K5 Max is added, the page is writable with angle C: what 'full size' means by each maker's key count (Keychron 108, Lofree 100 / 96%, NuPhy 99) plus polling rate by connection, with Keychron first and the Flow Lite 2 100 as the narrow, light alternative.
